Pure Bread Long fermented. Baked for the neighbourhood.

European sourdough, hand shaped pastries and specialty coffee on Honour Avenue, open since 3 October 2026.

Message on Instagram See the counter

The long ferment comes first

Pure Bread is built on long fermented European sourdough. The dough is given time, shaped by hand, and baked into loaves with a dark crust and an open crumb. It is the new Graceville bakery from Eddy Tice and Ania Kutek, and it opened its doors on Saturday 3 October 2026.

The morning bake

Keep scrolling and watch the morning bake rise into place, shelf by shelf, the way it does before the doors open.

The loaves settle in first, then the pastries find their places.

The case is full. This is the moment to be at the counter.

What is on the counter

Seven things, done properly. The range moves sideways as you scroll, like walking the length of the case.

Sourdough

Long fermented European style loaves with a dark, crisp crust and an open crumb.

Grilled sourdough toasties

Sourdough pressed on the grill until crisp, with a molten centre.

Chocolate hazelnut babka

A twisted loaf swirled through with chocolate and hazelnut.

Basque cheesecake

Caramelised on top, soft and custardy in the middle.

Croissants and pastries

Hand shaped pastries with fine, flaky layers.

Madeleines

Small shell shaped sponge cakes, golden at the edges.

Specialty coffee

Specialty coffee, poured to go with the bake.

For the day's bake and any questions, message the bakery on Instagram.

Sold out daily.

In its own posts, Pure Bread says the bake sells out daily. If there is a loaf or a slice of babka with your name on it, the early visit is the safe one, and an Instagram message is the way to ask.
